headline: Collect levels, then reverse their order
statement: Return a binary tree’s node values grouped by depth, starting with the deepest level and ending with the root. Within each level, keep left-to-right order. Trees use level-order arrays with null for absent children.
intuition: Collect the tree's levels from the root downward using a queue. Then reverse the list of levels. Reverse only the groups, keeping values within each group in left-to-right order. This gives the required bottom-up result with a simple, consistent traversal.
approach: Return an empty list for an absent root.
At each round process exactly the queue size measured at that round’s start.
Enqueue children left before right, save the level, and reverse the collected levels.
correctness: At the start of a round the queue holds exactly one depth in left-to-right order. Its children form the next depth in that same order. Reversing the depth groups gives deepest-to-root order while preserving each group’s ordering.
bruteForce: Run a separate depth-limited traversal for every depth; on a chain this revisits nodes and costs O(n²).

complexity.space: O(w + h) auxiliary plus O(n) output
complexity.explanation: Each node is visited once. The queue holds O(w) nodes across adjacent levels; the shallow outer reversal creates O(h) additional row references, while returned rows store all n values.

pitfalls: Freeze the queue size before adding children.
Do not use pop(0) on Python lists for the queue.
